reviews.reason: Internal examination and ordinary probing do not measure nutritional composition or identify chemical hazards. Develop a staged analytical capability, beginning with measured water and dry-residue fractions. A narrowly scoped protein-precipitating-compound screen may follow only with actual reagents, controls and validated detection limits. Your plum samples support sample preparation, but do not supply analytical equipment, reference materials or safety conclusions.
reviews.experienceReview: A successfully completed measurement establishing a genuinely new, supported observation can plausibly provide the existing confirmed-understanding experience. Subscribe food-assay's information-confirmed event to grounded-understanding, qualified only for the performing actor with completed paid measurements, valid calibration/controls, explicit uncertainty and a previously unverified finding. Reuse its 0.8 amount, cap 1, duration 8 rounds, refresh repetition and 12-round cooldown; maintained participation adds 0.035 within that same source's bounded saturation, with existing 0.0015 decay. Do not add an assay-specific duplicate source. Repeated measurements may improve evidence, but identical established findings do not qualify as new information. Application, equipment labels, learning, invalid runs and merely discovering missing prerequisites award nothing. No separate pleasure or mastery reward is established; health, hunger and toxin exposure remain governed by actual physical events.
reviews.visualReview: Render the constructed balance, its pans and allocated loads, drying tray and changing sample as persistent objects at their real positions. Show active handling only during paid work and show passive moisture loss only when the physical process advances. Replay assay-reading events as measured comparisons with resolution and uncertainty; completion displays residue, losses, controls and unresolved hazards, never a generic safe-food badge. Invalid or interrupted runs visibly preserve their actual partial samples and remaining-work record. Chemical-screen graphics appear only after real reagents and equipment have been supplied and used.
reviews.specification:
Implement food-assay@1 through the current Codex handoff, with executable precursor equipment preparation and gravimetric analysis; keep the chemical-screen mode explicitly unavailable until its stated dependencies are physically met. Reuse inventory, food provenance, process scheduling, geometry and information-confirmation code, not their functional equivalence IDs.
Public schema: object with required mode enum[prepare-balance,prepare-dryer,dry-mass,protein-precipitation], target string, apparatus string, controls array of item-ID strings; optional quantity number >=0.1 in supported inventory increments; additionalProperties=false. Shared references: target resolves once to an owned sample for assay modes or owned construction inputs for preparation; apparatus resolves to a persistent nearby apparatus; controls resolve to owned, provenance-bearing materials. Preparation uses explicit material allocations in the project record and must never silently select or create supplies.
Dependencies and precursor: add a small comparison balance and passive drying tray. A balance uses 1 branch, 1 vine and 0.4 bark, assembled over 4 work rounds at 1 energy/round, retaining all input mass in the apparatus. Equal-arm geometry, suspension and two pans must be represented; unsuitable branch geometry or failed suspension prevents completion rather than granting precision. A tray uses 0.4 bark over 2 work rounds at 0.5 energy/round. These are proposed products, not existing equipment. Comparison weights are actual retained stone pieces, made by paid subdivision with an owned hard stone tool: 2 rounds and 1 energy/round per batch, with fragments and waste conserving mass. Use relative comparison masses, not privileged item-mass readouts; record resolution, repeatability and calibration history. Calibration uses empty-pan zeroing, exchanged loads and repeated comparison against retained weights, 3 rounds at 0.5 energy/round. Without a traceable external standard, report mass ratios and uncertainty, not absolute certified grams.
Dry-mass method: escrow at least 0.1 owned food unit; obtain an initial balance reading, spread the same sample on the tray, then perform repeated drying and weighing. Initial preparation and each weighing cost one round and 0.5 energy. Drying advances each round from actual ambient temperature, humidity, sample surface area and moisture, with evaporated water transferred to the environmental water ledger. Implement the necessary moisture/thermal coupling; passive drying cannot remove nonvolatile solids or create nutrition. Use existing food moisture as model initialization, not as an observation returned directly to the actor. Keep food decay and contamination active. Completion requires three consecutive paid readings separated by actual drying intervals, stable within the calibrated balance resolution; otherwise report incomplete drying. Report observed mass loss and residual fraction with uncertainty and possible volatile-loss/contamination confounds. Do not call residual mass calories, digestible carbohydrate, protein or toxin absence. Return the actual altered residue with original nutrient and toxin totals conserved except for explicitly modeled real losses, and trace every loss to an output stream. The residue remains available to existing eating mechanics with its altered moisture and provenance; analysis itself supplies no nutrition.
Chemical-screen dependency contract: protein-precipitation requires actual clean vessels, measured solvent, a verified soluble-protein reagent, a characterized tannin reference, reagent blank and negative control, plus calibrated mass/volume or optical comparison equipment. No catalogue resource or appearance alone certifies these. Do not create reagents, references, water stock or an acquisition accomplishment during implementation. Until these dependencies have real production/acquisition and verification records, this mode returns missing prerequisites before reserving sample or charging work. Once satisfied, execute matched blank, negative, positive-reference and sample extractions at recorded concentrations, consuming 0.1 sample unit and actual allocated reagent/solvent quantities; 6 active rounds at 0.5 energy/round plus measured settling time. Record all extracts and waste. Report only protein-precipitating activity relative to the reference: this is a tannin-compatible hazard screen, not toxin identification. Detection limit is the lowest independently prepared reference dilution distinguished from blanks by the implemented measurement model; failed controls invalidate the run. No microbial, alkaloid or universal-safety claim follows from a negative result. Broader nutritional or hazard claims remain unmeasured.
Persistent state includes owner, sample lineage, apparatus IDs and calibration, allocated materials, readings, environmental history, assay stage, paid effort, actual remaining work, residues and waste. Place equipment in shared world geometry on unobstructed ground; apply actual footprint/collision and support constraints. Active handling requires distance <=0.65 from its interaction boundary; unattended passive drying follows real local conditions and remains physically accessible to interference. No room-wide drying, shade or insulation effects are implied. Global pauses freeze progress. Missing equipment, unsuitable weather or inadequate energy pauses without charging unperformed work. Movement/action change cancels active handling; explicit cancellation or death terminates that actor's multi-round operation and releases surviving escrow exactly once at the apparatus or valid ground position. Preserve altered material, spent work and losses; never restore the original sample or clone escrow. No automatic continuation after death.
Declare food-assay-started, assay-reading, food-assay-completed and assay-invalidated; also emit existing process-progress, process-stopped, trial-result and information-confirmed where appropriate.
